en:
Port town Milfe... Though on the frontier, it thrives as an independent city through maritime industry, ore mining, and trade. 
I, having finally reached this destination of my journey, halted as I stepped into its central plaza. The ship I had taken toward this city had run aground, forcing me to continue overland on foot. 
My body now feels a pleasant weariness, the relief of having arrived. Unused to fatigue, I found this fresh sensation unexpectedly delightful.
Fatigue has changed my body. I must reflect on this.
We finally arrived, Master.
Is something the matter, Master?

...............
(I had forgotten...
I should not push myself too hard...)
I'm a man, no doubt about it, but there's a slight swelling there that a man shouldn't have.

Hearing that voice, I close my chest and look up toward its source. A girl with a large pack on her back looks up at me. Her name is Shuri. Due to certain circumstances, she is a household servant who will accompany me on this journey. She became a war orphan long ago, and since I took her in, she has worked as a servant, mainly attending to me. Perhaps because she has been working in the house since childhood, she is especially obedient, devoted, and capable among the servants. Lately, however, she has matured and started to keep a step back from me, which leaves me feeling somewhat lonely...
Feeling something wrong, I open my shirt and look.
Yeah.
Right... Let us find an inn for now.
What shall we do now, Master?
Yes, I hope we can find a nice inn.
No, it's nothing...
Shuri is staring at me. That slightly anxious gaze of hers has not changed at all since I picked her up on the battlefield over ten years ago.
Of course.
Huh?
No, she's angry.
Ah, Miss Levia!
Levia presses in where Shuri stepped aside.
What?!
Celica! What the hell have you been doing?
The ship ran aground.
Shuri, is that true?
It didn't sink, but we walked all the way here.

Accompanied by several soldiers, a woman in silver armor glares at me as if about to shoot me dead. This woman is General Levia. She is the only female knight commander in Lewinia, where I am staying as a guest general, and also an old acquaintance. I was supposed to meet her in this city three days ago... It seems she is quite angry.
The scenery was nice...

Still, we arrived three days behind schedule...
I hope Levia is not angry, but...
Yeah.
Yes, Levia. Five days ago, the ship we were on ran aground and ended up on land.
...So you walked here?
Shuri, who is oblivious to such things as killing intent, spoke without noticing, and I answered with a sigh.
No, the mission's meaning is...
What do you think this mission is?!
For an instant, it felt as if the air itself had frozen. Shuri's neck shrank in dread of the fury Levia was about to unleash on me.
Levia's fierce shout rang out, and the people nearby froze in fear.
I hesitated... I could have taken a cart, but chose not to. She will be angry. Shuri looked confused. Lying would fail because she is too honest and would anger Levia more. I had to tell the truth.
Disgrace, huh...
My frank reply to her needle-sharp, icy question made Levia's slender eyebrows rise in anger.
We are searching for the missing Princess Ratina?

Shuri answered, as if making an excuse for me.
Levia, who had often visited my mansion
and knew Shuri never lied, slowly nodded.
It was you who killed that monster.

She is enshrined deep within the royal palace as a living goddess. To give us a chance to recuperate, she issued this mission in the form of an oracle, sending us out of the country still in postwar turmoil. But it seems Levia didn't get that memo, and she's been overly enthusiastic to a fault. Even the tip that started this mission is nothing but a dubious story about a princess who went missing eighteen years ago being spotted in this town, looking exactly as she did back then...
I couldn't have defeated it alone.
If Shuri says it, it must be true, but then why did you walk? You could have borrowed a horse or carriage in a village along the way.

You...
The Water Maiden gave us this: clear our disgrace.
Even if those nobles don't acknowledge it, you took down a monster that alone could rival an entire army. That's hardly a shame worth clearing.

A short while ago, there was a war between Levia's homeland, the country of Lewinia where I am currently staying as a guest commander, and a neighboring nation. At that time, Levia's White Earth Dragon Knights and I fought a giant demon that was the enemy's trump card, which was attempting to assault the royal capital from a different direction than the main force. Though we suffered many casualties, we destroyed it. However, unlike Levia and me who actually fought, those who only saw the demon's corpse, especially the nobles who knew nothing of battle, blamed Levia for losing so many soldiers, saying her command was poor... Due to the grievous wounds I sustained in that battle, I lost much of my power and could not participate in subsequent fighting, so I was deemed utterly useless. The only one who properly recognized our efforts was the great guardian deity of Lewinia and my ally, the Water Maiden.
Where to?
Alright.
Ah... I am sorry. Forget what I just said.

For now, I will tell you what we have found so far.
Follow me.
What happened?
Shut up! You're the one who finished it off. I... I just got my soldiers killed for nothing...

Levia... The lives lost in battle...
Calling them a waste does not sit well with me.
As headquarters for the princess search... I commandeered the local lord's manor.
From beside the silent Levia, a man stepped forward.
Perhaps embarrassed by her own thoughtless remark, Levia's anger suddenly cooled and she turned on her heel as if to hide her face.
A princess, fourth in line to the throne, who disappeared eighteen years ago. Even if we find her, I doubt she'd be any use as a political bargaining chip...
Lord Celica, regarding that matter, it was carried out by a group of common-born knights who admired General Levia.
Ranzabu shook his head from side to side, as if to say he was troubled.

Seeing Levia about to start walking, I asked a casual question while dodging Shuri, who, despite already carrying a lot of luggage, still tried to take the load I was holding. The hesitant answer that came back was an unexpected one.
In the end, we paid the local lord appropriate compensation and agreed to rent the mansion. However, because those common-born knights lacked foresight, we are now treated as invaders in this city.
Indeed, the eyes of the townspeople watching us since earlier hold little warmth.
Enough, Lord Ranzabu, it is all over...
Indeed... I should not have spoken out of turn. Forgive me.

Commandeering and looting are things Levia hates most. Furthermore, the city of Milfe, which we have come to under the pretext of searching for the princess, is not Lewinia territory, and such an act could be seen as an act of aggression.
So, we are going to that mansion now?
Lord Ranzabu... He serves as vice-commander of Levia's knight order, but... he is a man of endless dark rumors.
From their perspective, I'm sure they only wanted to ensure General Levia had a comfortable environment in which to do her work... But,
Yes.
Levia...
Go on ahead. I will find an inn.
It will be fine...
Then... No, I see. Understood...

Levia showed a brief, wounded look, but the next moment she turned on her heel and briskly departed. I understood what Levia wanted to say. That manor likely had rooms prepared for us... Still, I felt bad for Levia, but I did not want to get involved in unnecessary trouble. Levia probably knew that, which is why she left without another word. Shuri stared at Levia as she departed.
Master?
Yes, that is true.
Ah, yes, indeed. Then I shall go look for an inn, Master...
First, let's decide on an inn.
Though I was short on words, that one remark seemed to have wiped away a little anxiety from Shuri's face. Turning to face me, Shuri is waiting for my next words.
There is no need. Let us go into that inn.
Huh?

As Shuri turned, the sign reading "Wild Bull's Hoof Inn" reflected in her eyes. At first glance, the establishment looked like a simple eatery, but judging by the size of the building, it seemed they also offered lodging. Seeing me start walking toward the Wild Bull's Hoof Inn, Shuri quickly got ahead of me and opened the door. I passed in front of her and stepped inside, where the fragrant smell of roasting meat filled the air.
Um, excuse me, is the owner of this shop...

Ranzabu's words carry a subtle tone of reproach toward Levia. A snake in the grass... I hear that this man Ranzabu was raised to his current position by nobles who are displeased that a woman like Levia is a general... It is very likely that he had a hand in the matter of those knights who admire Levia as well. After bowing obsequiously to Levia as she turned back, Ranzabu resumed his place behind her as before.

"Welcome!"
The cheerful greeting from a female employee
was the first thing we heard upon entering.
"Two, right? Those seats are free."
Lunchtime had the place nearly full.
She looked around, then pointed to two empty
counter seats.
Ah, s-sorry!
Yes.
Ah, no, I mean... do you have any rooms available?

The shopkeeper:
Being called "Master" tickles me,
but that's me.

...! As I surveyed the square for an inn, a sudden, piercing bloodlust struck me. Turning, I saw a familiar figure emerge from a nearby diner, shoulders stiff with anger, charging at me with huge strides. That was...

Female Shopkeeper:
Hehe, you don't need to apologize.
So, what can I do for you?

Levia, a female general, bears needless burdens. Shuri cannot understand this, not knowing the military, and feels helpless. She watches Levia leave, worry on her face. ...It seems I will not rest easy here.

When we came to the empty counter seats,
the female owner went behind the counter,
pulled out a guestbook, and faced us.
She said, "Sorry, I'm Rinsha. What're your names?"
Yes.
Rinsha smoothly writes our names in the register.

N-No, it's not like that.
Um, separate rooms, please...
A servant? That explains your outfit.
Rinsha tilts her head at the flustered Shuri.
Yes, this is Master Celica Sylphil, and I am his servant, Shuri.
The innkeeper says, "So you are a guest at the inn? Then come over to the counter."
So, about the room... We have a double room available. A double room?

Oh, really?
Then, rooms next to each other?
Yes, please.
So, how many nights will you be staying?
Um...
Not sure how long, but for now, one week.
Hearing my voice from behind Shuri, Rinsha's face is replaced by a surprised expression.
Oh, you're a man?
Yeah.
Ohhh...

For a certain reason, I have the kind of looks that
can easily be mistaken for a woman's.
Um...
Rinsha stared at my face as if it were something rare, and Shuri spoke to her with a troubled tone.
Hm? Oh, right, right. We charge upfront, that okay?
Yes, how much will it be?
Two rooms for a week, so... 140 shillings.
Shuri's hand, which had been opening the travel money pouch, instantly froze.
What's wrong?
Shirin... is that...?
That's right... Oh! Could it be you don't have any?
Yes, because until now we could pay with Ludra...
Come to think of it, when we were leaving Lewinia, Levia did mention that the currency used in this town is different...
Oh, in this town you can't use Rudora.
I will go exchange some money.
That won't work.
Eh?
Three days ago, the Lewinia army came through, and all of them cashed in at once, so the exchange is just overflowing with Rudora now.
Huh?!
So yesterday, all the currency exchange people left, saying they would exchange their money in another town.
That's...

Shuri was flustered; I laid a hand on her shoulder
and stepped forward before Rinsha at the shop.
Ah, Master...
Will this cover it?
I casually held out a jewel I took from my inner pocket.
What is this? Could it be a gem?

It's no wonder she finds it strange. The gem,
redder than blood, shining with cloudless clarity,
is larger than her wide-open eyes.
It's surely worth a year of leisure, though.
Are you planning to buy this entire inn?
Not at all.
In that case... I can't accept a gem this valuable.
Consider it a down payment.
A deposit?
If we leave without paying the inn bill, that jewel is yours.
So if I pay, you'll give back the jewel?
Right.
Got it. Then forget about just a week - you can stay as long as you like.
Yeah, I'll take you up on that.
Rinsha walks toward the stairs leading to the second floor.
Um, Master...
What is it?
Was that all right? That gem was a very expensive one, given to us by the Water Priestess...
Was it?
Yes, it was certainly worth enough for a person to live in leisure for a lifetime, but...
Master?
Where are you going, Master?

After Rinsha showed me to my room, I checked the escape routes just in case. Finally at ease, I took a good look around the room that would be mine for the time being. It was a pleasant room, clean and bright with good sunlight. From this second-floor window, I had a full view of the plaza at the heart of the city. A far cry from the cheap inns I used to stay at during my days on the run... My mind drifted back to those times, unbidden... It was many decades ago now. For a certain reason, I once fought a goddess who was said to have vanished into the heavens in ancient times. Against a goddess whose power should have been absolute, I miraculously managed to fight to a draw and claim victory. I sealed the goddess's will, and since my own body had been mortally wounded in the battle, I survived by taking that goddess's body as my own... That... was the beginning of everything...

The god I defeated was a being called an evil god, hostile to the gods who rule this world now. But it was still a god, and because I defeated it and took its power, other gods and their followers called me "God Slayer" and feared me, trying to erase my existence. Over the following decades, since I had obtained a goddess's body and stopped aging, I spent my days fighting and fleeing from most of the world. Eventually, I formed an alliance with the sole god of the great nation of Levia, the "Water Maiden," who belongs to no faction, and gained a temporary haven... For over ten years after that, within Levia, where the Water Maiden is the state religion, attempts on my life by other gods and their followers grew less frequent. But if my true identity were to become known in this town that does not belong to Levia, all its residents would become my enemies, and I would be hunted until I could flee back to Levia. The room is furnished with a lockable chest for belongings, suggesting it is intended for long-term stays.

Lost in thought, I suddenly remembered and retrieved a sheathed short sword from my luggage beside the bed. Though it lacked grand ornamentation, it bore smooth, feminine curves and a subdued design. The moment I held it, a languid young woman's voice echoed in my mind.
(What, you finally made it?)
(Yeah)
I answer. The voice is the dagger I hold. Haishera is sealed inside. He sought my power but lost. I defeated and sealed him. Since then, he's been my sword. Weakened, using him could cost my mind...

Still, leaving me shut in your luggage...
is a bit too cruel, don't you think?
(Sorry, forgot)
(You, my Master...)
I set Haishera at my side and looked around again.
( Hmm, a good room for a frontier town. )
Through my eyes, Haishera saw the room and, unusually, praised it. Compared to cheap inns I use without Shuri, like now... that might be why.
Yeah, nice room.
Hehe, thanks.
I meant to answer Haishera, but I accidentally muttered aloud. Rinsha, holding fresh sheets, smiled at me from the doorway.

Now, once you drop off your luggage, go get Shuri
and head to the dining hall downstairs. You're hungry, right?

I hadn't noticed until she mentioned it.
But I haven't eaten since we got here.
Is that fine?
No problem, I will put it on your tab.

Saying that, Rinsha took out the jewel from her chest and showed it to me. Rinsha and I left the room on the second floor and came down the stairs together. Afterwards, Shuri came to check on my room without being asked, saw the sheets in Rinsha's hands, and offered to do the cleaning and bed-making herself. At first, Rinsha politely declined, but overwhelmed by Shuri's pleading attitude, she accepted the offer.
What a peculiar child...
Perhaps recalling the delighted smile Shuri had when receiving the sheets, Rinsha speaks to me with a complex smile.
That girl's the hardest worker in the house.
Oh, there are other servants?
Mm.

Hmm, you have so many servants...
Celica, could you be a noble?
No.
Then who are you?

Without answering her question of who I was, I sat at a nearby table in the dining hall, which was starting to empty after the lunch hour. Perhaps judging that I did not want to talk, Rinsha brought a menu from the counter and placed it in front of me without a word.
I guarantee it tastes good.

Rinsha, beaming broadly,
puffed out her ample chest even more.
Indeed, the scent of cooking that fills this hall
is enough to whet my appetite.

Yeah...
Something light, and not a lot of it.
You want something girly, huh... then this one.
Rinsha points her finger at a dish on the menu.
I see.
So, Shuri-chan...
Coming.

As soon as I said that, Shuri came down the stairs
with quiet yet hurried steps.
Oh, really...
Quietly hurried footsteps... As a child, Shuri would often run up to me. I warned her she might trip and get hurt, so ever since she has walked like this.
I am sorry to have kept you waiting...
It's fine, right, Celica?
Yeah.
So, Shuri-chan, what are you having?
Ah, I'll have mine after Master.
Saying so, Shuri stood diagonally behind me.
What's the matter, Shuri?
Rinsha calls out to Shuri with a curious look.
Yes, I will serve you.
A waitress...?
Rinsha turns her sharp glare on me.
Shuri, take a seat.
But, Master...

This is the usual exchange...
Shuri always insists on serving me whenever we go out to eat.
Left to her, she does it perfectly, but--
It's one thing at the mansion; in a restaurant, it stands out far too much...
That's right, Shuri. The food here isn't so hard to eat that you need to stand there serving. And it'd be sad to make Master eat all alone, don't you think?
Shuri.
Yes, certainly...

At my urging, Shuri finally stepped away from me.
Her movements were awkward as she took her seat.
She did not seem reluctant; she was tense.
I will have this.
I looked at Shuri, her cheeks flushed and head hung low, and pointed to the dish on the menu that Rinsha had told me about.
Yes, and what'll you have, Shuri?
Ah, then I'll have the same as Master...
Another typical Shuri reaction.
I see...
Rinsha gave a slow nod, then lightly elbowed me in the back and headed to the kitchen.
Hm?
Before long, Rinsha returned with food for three.
I haven't eaten yet either. Mind if I join you?
She says that while already setting the table for three.
Yeah
Thanks.
As soon as I answered, Rinsha, who had been sitting across from me with a pleasant smile, bombarded me with questions in rapid succession...
So, what brings you two to this town?
Recuperation.
Oh, but weren't you just talking with Levia out front?
Does Levia come here often?
Yeah, she's a regular lately... wait, I knew it.
What about?
The guy who never shows up... That is you, Celica.
Did Levia say that?
She sure was. She was pretty mad, like "What do you think the mission is?"
I already heard that.
Rinsha laughs merrily.
So, Celica, you came to look for someone too, right?
Half of it's recuperation.
My, you are not taking this seriously, are you? And Levia is working so hard.
Yeah.
Levia is certainly diligent, but she tends to overdo it. I hope that does not work against her.
What do you think of Levia and the others?
Huh? They are guests.
Rinsha answers my sudden question naturally.
That's not it... Levia isn't well liked in this town.
Ah, right... worried?
More or less.
Heh heh, it's fine. When she first arrived, there was some fuss, but Levia herself is quite popular with the townsfolk, you know.
That so?

Yes, she is. Even with a title like general,
she is polite to the townspeople.
And most of all, being a beauty,
many admire her, especially girls.
I see...

Certainly, Levia is a woman who became a general, so while she may be resented by some men, she is hugely popular among women. When she was at the Lewinia royal palace, I often saw her being constantly followed by the daughters of nobles and looking greatly troubled.
But...
What?
It seems you are not getting along with the town watch.
A vigilante group?
Yes, they're mercenaries the lord of this town hired for emergencies when Levia's group arrived.
By 'emergency'... you mean if Levia and the others were to occupy this city?
That is right. I keep saying Levia would not do that, but the vigilantes hired for that very reason are hostile toward Levia and her group.
I see...

After the meal, I popped the last parsley garnish
on my plate into my mouth and stood up.
I will work just enough to avoid Levia scolding.
Seeing me stand, Shuri, who had already finished eating, also rose from her seat and looked at me.
Master
I will return by evening. Do as you like.
Yes, Master.
Shuri answered without hesitation, and Rinsha also stood up from her seat.
Well, I guess I'll get back to work too.
Saying that, she began clearing away the dishes.
Take care, Master.
I pass by Shuri as she holds the door open and bows, stepping out into the central plaza that the shop faces. As I walk away, I hear her voice calling from inside, where she has returned.
Rinsha, please let me help...
Goodness, what a diligent girl...

Looking from the square, I see a particularly
large building to the north. That is likely
the Lords Manor. The square overflows with a
motley crowd. I must visit Levia for now...
(Where are you going?)
To Levia.
（Hoh, that maiden... From what I have heard, she seems to be taking on needless troubles yet again.）

(Ah, I wonder what reason there could be
to stay in the army after such hardship.)
How dull you are, Master...
What does she mean?
Heh... I wouldn't be so boorish...
(Won't Levia get angry if we don't hurry?)
Yeah...
Ah, Master, welcome back.
Welcome back...? Wait, you just left. Did you forget something?
No...
Then what is it?
......I am off.
Please take care, Master.
You're a weird kid...
If I keep Levia waiting too long, she will get angry. I should hurry to the lord's manor.
I headed to the big mansion north of town.
Sorry to have kept you waiting.

I was shown to a room in the mansion.
Levia and an unusually tall young man came in.
It has been a while, Celica.

This friendly youth with narrow eyes is Refin,
Levia's most trusted subordinate.
He alone can stop her when she lashes out at me.
Refin, are you feeling better?
Refin had shielded Levia with his own body in the fight against the demons the enemy set loose during the last war. He should have been terribly wounded, but...
Yes, I'm completely better now.

Concerned that his head might brush the ceiling, Refin slightly crouches and shows off by moving his arm. Perhaps due to his massive build, he truly recovers quickly, and he's so resilient it's hard to believe he's human. There was no need for me to worry...
Don't push yourself yet.
Levia gently admonishes Refin.
Oh, I am sorry.
Levia is serious and strict, but outside of battle, she is gentle...
Now then, the investigation results...
When she turned to face me, her expression held not just severity but even hostility.
What?
No... never mind.

Levia gave her report in a businesslike manner.
In summary, a person resembling Princess Latina,
who went missing eighteen years ago, was sighted.
She vanished in an abandoned mine 1 km from town.

So we will start investigating
that abandoned mine tomorrow...

At that point, Levia cut off her words, and silence fell over the room. It seemed her report was not yet finished, but whenever she tried to speak, she hesitated and faltered. ...It appeared there was something hard for her to say. Levia was staring at me, almost glaring.
Ah...
Suddenly, Levia met my eyes. She blushed and looked away.
W-Wait, where are you going?
I have no particular place in mind. But we look for Princess Latina, do we not?
...I still have reports to finish.
I see. Then continue.
Go on.
So?

At my prompting, Levia's face flushes,
but it is not entirely from anger.
Something seems... off.

General Levia, I will take the report from here.
Could you please go check on the troops?
Refin, unable to bear watching Levia's state, called out to throw her a lifeline. But Levia hesitated for a moment at his words, then stared me straight in the eye.

Fine, I will report first.
It concerns the princess sighted in this town...
Something wrong?

Quiet! It's about Princess Latina...
She comes out at night and attacks men,
sucking out their... essence.
Life force? Like a succubus?
Yes...
Sleep demons are a general term for demons that appear as a woman before men and as a man before women, engage in nightly intimacies, and absorb the life energy known as essence from their partners.

That is my report. You would do well
to avoid falling victim yourself.
Levia rushed through the rest of her report and then hurried out of the room, as if to hide her blushing face.
Still such a novice when it comes to this...
Indeed.

Left behind by Levia, Refin narrowed his already
thin eyes and nodded in agreement.
I found myself recalling the old Levia...
Over a decade ago, I received a mansion in
Lewinia's royal capital. As ally to Water Maiden,
ready to lend strength if necessary, I had just
a brief peace. Then Levia and Refin appeared.
Both were born to knightly families. Refin admired
my strength. Levia, in a white dress with a
fleeting smile and a white flower, always by my
side, as if to soothe my heart, smiled...
Several years passed. Through my pact
with the Water Maiden, I went to many battles,
and returned from deadly battles. What greeted me
was Levia in armor, with sword and resolute eyes.
Celica?

I shook my head to clear my thoughts. Refin was bending over, gazing down at me. Refin is so tall that, in ordinary buildings, his head would hit the ceiling. So, this slightly hunched posture has become a habit for him. This room appears to be a guest room in the lord's mansion. They put me here, not the reception room, likely to avoid using the room with valuable furnishings.
What's the matter, Celica?
Refin watches me with probably puzzled eyes as I look around restlessly.
It's nothing. Tell Levia I'll also be going to that abandoned mine starting tomorrow.

Yes, I understand.
It is reassuring that you are coming, Celica-san.
Later.
Yes, thank you for your hard work.
When I returned to the central plaza, a crowd had gathered in one corner, and from the alley beyond, I could hear a woman's rough but spirited voice. It looked like a fight.
Welcome back, Master.
Oh, you are back already? It is still early for dinner.
Have a safe trip, Master.

Beyond the crowd, an alleyway hosts a brawl. Too many people block my view from here. The narrow passage overflows with gawkers and is in chaos. The inn itself is deserted, even though it is not mealtime, customers are scarce. They have likely all gone to watch the fight.

Suddenly the customers stopped coming.
I wonder if something happened outside?
Looks like a fight over there.
A fight? In the alley over there?
Yeah, that's right.
That girl again, huh...
That girl?
That alley there's got a super hot-headed girl.
Oh well, I guess I'll take a break until the customers who went to gawk come back. Shuri, let's have some tea.
Ah, um, Master...
I have more to do. You should rest.
Yes, Master.

Shuri and Rinsha are preparing tea. It would be rude to interrupt. The room is probably thanks to Shuri--it is even cleaner than when I first entered, and the luggage from the floor has been neatly stowed away. A crowd still lingers in a corner of the plaza visible from the window. It is still too early to sleep...
I slipped through the crowd of onlookers and arrived at the back alley where the fight was taking place.
What did you say?! Say that again!
I see Lewinian knights of Levia and a tall redhead with a greatsword glaring at each other.

I will say it again:
you frontier savages have no business
lecturing us Lewinian knights! Know your place!
What?!
As the knight spoke, the woman facing him seethed with killing intent. She reached for the hilt of the sword on her back. Seeing this, the knights grinned and moved to draw their own blades.
What are you doing?
Ugh... Celica... Silfil...

As I thought... Seeing the knights step back when I intervened, I was convinced. Their armor was the same as Levia's subordinates', but these men are not Levia's direct subordinates. Because of Levia's personality as a leader, her direct knights all value politeness; unless the other party is an enemy, they never speak vulgarly. Moreover, since I formally saved Levia in the previous war, they would not address me so rudely. Their arrogant way of speaking and the way they back away when they see me... these men were probably temporarily transferred from another unit for this mission.
You! Are you protecting that woman?!

Protect?
I am just asking what you are doing.
Tch...

Their silence shows they know they are at fault.
I see knights holding fruit, a local treat.
The nearby fruit stall owner is watching
anxiously this way, which suggests
the knights took it without payment.
Who are you?
A red-haired woman is giving me a suspicious look.
Just passing through.

As our gazes broke, the knights
hurried off, faces hidden by their helmets.
Woman! I will let you off today.
What the--!
The red-haired woman spat out a parting curse fit for a thug. She took a step as if to chase the fleeing knights, but quickly stopped herself, perhaps thinking it pointless.
Tch, what is going on...

Fruit Stand
Sorry, Kaura.
